target_customer: Large employers hiring graduates and early-career talent, who pay for a screening and ranking platform
problem: Employers screen large volumes of applicants on experience and qualifications, which is slow and biased, while candidates refill the same application forms repeatedly.
product_category: AI recruiting and candidate screening software

founders.name: Nicholas Shekerdemian
education: Dropped out of college (school not named in TechCrunch 2017; a secondary profile says Oxford, unverified)
previous_startups: Online business matching English teachers with Chinese citizens (TechCrunch 2017), outcome not stated
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO, with a bio mentioning TVC as founding partner.

founders.name: Jeremy Hindle
founders.background_notes: Described as technical co-founder by TechCrunch 2017. No background given.

competitors.name: Koru
competitors.what: Talent marketplace that assessed graduates for fit with employers

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching and scoring candidates with machine learning needed data science and bias handling, but used standard ML tooling in 2017 and was built by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise recruiting integrations create some stickiness, but screening algorithms and forms were copyable and many assessment vendors existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. A small OTC listed holding company bought it in all stock in August 2022.

market_need_then: Graduate recruiters wanted to widen and de-bias screening, and applicants disliked repetitive forms (TechCrunch 2017). Demand specifics beyond that were not sourced.

branding.domain_note: Uses headstart.io; the exact .com history was not found.

identity.visual_style: Marketing site tagline: a recruiting platform with real impact
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions around fairness, diversity and potential over pedigree

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself. The name is a common phrase that collides with the US Head Start program and Headstarter, which hurts search distinctiveness.

outcome_analysis: Headstart grew to enterprise clients such as Accenture, Vodafone and Expedia according to the acquirer's release, then sold in August 2022 for a reported 14 million dollars in stock to a small OTC listed holding company. That price and buyer suggest a modest outcome rather than a venture scale exit. Founders stayed on as board members after the deal. Funding history is unclear from reliable sources.
notes: Unverified funding: Dealroom and Seedtable list a seed of about 7 million USD in 2019-11 (another aggregator says 5 million in 2019-09 and another 7 million in 2018-11), five rounds and about 7.12 million total; no investor names tied to rounds. A Sifted article on a 7 million round was blocked (403). CB Insights lists Silverback United, Founders Factory, FoundersX Ventures and Plug and Play as investors without round detail. Founded year 2015 and co-founders per Dealroom and the Silverback release. Exit amount 14 million is as press-reported all-stock value. Education of Shekerdemian: only 'dropped out' is sourced from opened TechCrunch article.
